transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I keep getting stuck on these thoughts that I might have missed something important. Like… a wrong number in a data release, or maybe I didn’t lock the back door, or I paid a bill from the wrong account. Even when I know I checked, I can’t seem to let go of the idea that I caused some kind of disaster.
Do you feel the need to do anything to try and get rid of these thoughts?

Yes. I… I check things. A lot.

I’ll reopen spreadsheets, reread emails line by line, check the locks, payment confirmations… usually in the same order. I keep doing it until it feels safe enough, I guess. Sometimes I’m still sitting at my desk hours later and I haven’t really gotten anything done.
Do you feel like you have to check things in a specific way or order to feel okay?

Yes… I do. It has to be in a certain order, or it doesn’t feel settled.

I’ll reopen the spreadsheet, then reread the email line by line, then check the lock or the payment confirmation… sometimes more than once. I keep going until it feels safe enough. Some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, and I haven’t actually finished anything.
Do you feel like checking things helps prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… in the moment it feels like if I check it the right way, then I’m stopping something bad from happening. Like if I reopen the spreadsheet, reread the email, check the lock or the payment confirmation in the right order, then maybe it’s safe.

But it doesn’t really end there. I keep doing it over and over, and some nights I’m still at my desk hours later with nothing actually finished.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts and the need to check things?
I’m not really sure. It feels like it’s been… a long time, but I don’t know when it actually started. I guess I noticed it more recently, but I couldn’t give you a date.
Do you feel anxious when you're unable to check things in the way you want to?

Yes. I get really uneasy if I can’t do it the way I need to.

I’ll end up reopening the spreadsheet, rereading the email line by line, checking the lock or the payment confirmation… in that order, usually. If I don’t, it just doesn’t feel safe. And then I keep going until I calm down a little, even if it takes hours.
Do you feel the need to perform any physical actions, like tapping or touching things, in a specific way to relieve your anxiety?

Not really tapping, no. It’s more… checking things in a certain order.

I’ll reopen the spreadsheet, reread the email line by line, check the lock or the payment confirmation again and again until it feels safe enough. Sometimes that goes on for hours, and I don’t actually get much finished.
Has this need to check things interfered with your daily routine or relationships?

Yes… it has. Work especially. I’ve missed or fallen behind on some big deadlines because I stay late checking and reviewing things, but I still don’t really finish.

And I’ve stopped going to things I used to do, like salsa nights or kayaking, because I can’t get away from the checking in time.
Do you feel like your checking is aimed at preventing something specific from happening to yourself or others?

Yes… sort of. It feels like if I don’t check, something could be wrong and I’ll miss it.

So I reopen spreadsheets, reread emails line by line, check locks or payment confirmations… usually in a certain order. I keep doing it until it feels safe enough. Some nights I’m still at my desk hours later, and nothing is actually finished.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or images that disturb you and aren't related to checking things?

I don’t think so. Not that I’ve really noticed.

It’s mostly the checking that gets stuck in my head.
How much distress do these thoughts and the need to check things cause you?

A lot. I don’t really like saying that, but… it can take over.

I’ll reopen spreadsheets, reread emails line by line, check locks or payment confirmations in the same order, over and over, just to calm down. And some nights I’m still sitting there hours later, with nothing actually finished.
Have your checking habits affected your relationships with family or friends?

A little, yes. I’ve… missed things with friends mostly.

I used to go to salsa nights, and kayaking sometimes, but I often can’t leave on time because I’m still checking or reviewing something. And work has been affected too—I’ve fallen behind on big deadlines because I stay late going over things and still don’t actually finish.
Do you believe that your checking habits are necessary to prevent harm to yourself or others?

I guess part of me feels like I have to, yes.

Like if I don’t reopen the spreadsheet, or reread the email line by line, or check the lock or payment confirmation in the right order, I can’t settle. It doesn’t feel safe yet. So I keep going until it calms down… even if I’m still there hours later and nothing’s really finished.
Have you had to turn down social invitations or opportunities because of your need to check things?

Yes… I have. Mostly things like salsa nights or kayaking. I’ll mean to go, but then I’m still checking or reviewing something, and I just… can’t get out the door in time.

It’s happened with work too. I stay late going over things and still don’t finish, so I’ve fallen behind on some major deadlines.
